Flight Phase

โหมดโรลเอาท์

A mode of the autopilot or autoland system engaged after touchdown, controlling the aircraft's direction and deceleration along the runway centerline until low speed is reached.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

A mode of the autopilot or autoland system engaged after touchdown, controlling the aircraft's direction and deceleration along the runway centerline until low speed is reached.

Operational example

Upon touchdown, the autopilot entered roll-out mode, maintaining centerline until manual control resumed at taxi speed.

Localized term
